answer: A sybil clone registers as one opal. The copper is one ordered work chain that anchors identity, and each ember is one unit of work judged by the copper. Admitting an opal requires a proof bound to that opal and rejudging every earlier chain entry, so the $k$th opal burns $k^2$ ember. One proof cannot certify two opals and all clones must enter the same lane, so $n$ clones cost about $n^3/3$ ember attached to the single chain. Call this ordered-chain proof. It breaks if the copper can fork into private lanes or skip rejudging.
